Every torus Fourier moment of the entire differences law corresponds to an iid product of Fourier coefficients with zero total exponent. Coprimality forces p r_p+q r_q=0 so nonzero phase balance requires at least p+q nonzero entries. Exactly q frequencies +p and p frequencies -q produce (a/2)^q(b/2)^p exp(i p phi). The m=2 difference law yields a²/4 and b²/4, fixing positive amplitudes; p-fold phase recovers the rotation class. Reflection conjugates it, so p=2 phases 0 and pi/2 are inequivalent. Support integral A=(1/2) integral h rho confirms area, width cancels odd q mode, perimeter 2pi. Independent integer support enumeration for (2,3),(2,5),(3,4) confirms first possible phase imbalance precisely at p+q; full proof is the integer argument, not enumeration.

value.rationale: A sharp, arbitrarily-high observation-order information obstruction for natural convex geometric measurements with strictly positive curvature, despite matching standard perimeter/area/width observables. Unlike bare sparse-signal phase ambiguity, it constructs genuine noncongruent convex shapes and precisely identifies their first separating geometric observation order.

final_claim: Sparse analytic strictly convex support functions with coprime p<q harmonics have complete m-sample relative outward normal-angle laws independent of phase for m<p+q; a first nonzero phase-sensitive invariant occurs at exactly p+q and determines shape phase modulo rotation. Explicit p=2 odd-q pairs yield noncongruent smooth ovals sharing all lower-order relative laws, perimeter, area, and directional width.
limitations: Positive a,b and a+b<1 guarantee curvature; p,q coprime with 2<=p<q.
Shape up to rigid rotations/translations in family, not reconstruction of arbitrary convex curves from fixed finite order.
